original.reason: It covers both common conventions for natural numbers, but has decisive gaps/errors. For y=4k+2>=6, the mod-32 residues can be 0 as well as 16 (e.g. 7+25≡0), so exact 2-adic valuation 4 is not established. Also mod 256 yields only x≡3 (mod 16), not x=3. The m=0 factor argument also asserts without proof that the cofactor has a non-7 prime divisor.
